cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException thrown because Message is null
cases.description: Verify that the method validates the Message argument and throws an exception when it is null, regardless of the other parameters.

cases.expected: No exception; a new TSIGRecord is generated and added to the Message with a full signature
cases.description: When the old TSIGRecord is null the method should generate a fresh TSIGRecord. The fullSignature flag should cause the MAC to cover the entire message.

input.value: Message containing a single question section

cases.expected: Message contains a TSIGRecord whose MAC is computed over the whole wire format of the message (including the additional section)
cases.description: When fullSignature is true the MAC must be calculated over the complete message. The test extracts the TSIGRecord from the Message and recomputes the MAC using the same key to verify it matches.

input.value: Message with question and answer sections

cases.expected: Message contains a TSIGRecord whose MAC is computed only over the DNS header and the question section (the default TSIG behaviour)
cases.description: When fullSignature is false the MAC should be calculated over the minimal part of the message as defined by RFC 2845. The test validates that the MAC does not include the answer section.

input.value: Message with an existing TSIGRecord (old) attached
the same TSIGRecord that is already attached to the Message

cases.expected: The old TSIGRecord is replaced by a new TSIGRecord with an updated MAC and timestamp, preserving the original key name and algorithm
cases.description: When an existing TSIGRecord is supplied the method must re‑sign the message, updating the MAC and the time‑signed field while keeping other fields unchanged.

cases.expected: UnsupportedOperationException (or IllegalArgumentException) thrown because the algorithm cannot be mapped to a known HMAC implementation
cases.description: The apply method should validate the algorithm name. Supplying an unknown algorithm must result in a clear exception rather than silent failure.

input.value: Message whose timestamp is set to Instant.now().minus(TSIG.FUDGE).minusSeconds(1)

cases.expected: TSIGRecord added to the Message with a time‑signed value that is within the allowed fudge window (i.e., not older than FUDGE seconds)
cases.description: Even though the message timestamp is older than the current time, the apply method must adjust the time‑signed field to be within the allowed fudge period.

input.value: Message containing a question and answer section but no additional records
valid TSIGRecord with algorithm HMAC_SHA256 and key "testkey"

cases.expected: A TSIGRecord is appended to the message’s additional section; the MAC is calculated over the DNS header and the question section only (per RFC 2845). No existing additional records are disturbed.
cases.description: Ensures that `apply` correctly adds a TSIG record when the message has no prior additional records and that the MAC covers only the required parts when `fullSignature` is false.

group: Old TSIGRecord with different key name

input.value: Message that already contains a TSIGRecord with key name "old.example."
TSIGRecord with key name "new.example.", algorithm HMAC_SHA1, same secret as the existing TSIG

cases.expected: The existing TSIGRecord is replaced by a new one whose key name matches the supplied `old` record ("new.example.") and whose MAC is recomputed using the new key name. All other fields (algorithm, error code) are preserved from the supplied `old` record.
cases.description: Verifies that when an old TSIGRecord with a different key name is supplied, `apply` discards the previously attached TSIG and signs the message with the new key name.

input.value: Message with a single question section
TSIGRecord built with algorithm name "HMAC-MD5.SIG-ALG.REG.INT." and secret "md5key"

cases.expected: A TSIGRecord is added; its MAC is the MD5‑based HMAC of the header and question section. No exception is thrown, confirming legacy algorithm handling.
cases.description: Checks that the deprecated HMAC‑MD5 algorithm is still recognised and that a correct MAC is produced.

input.value: TSIGRecord with algorithm HMAC_SHA256 and an empty (zero‑length) secret key

cases.expected: TSIGRecord is added; the MAC consists of the HMAC‑SHA256 of the message using an empty key (which is a defined value, not an error). No exception is thrown.
cases.description: Ensures that the method can handle a secret key of length zero without crashing, as allowed by the underlying JCE implementation.

group: Empty Message (no sections) with fullSignature true

input.value: Message created with the default constructor and no sections added
valid TSIGRecord with algorithm HMAC_SHA384 and secret "emptymsg"

cases.expected: A TSIGRecord is appended; the MAC is computed over the DNS header only (since there are no question/answer/additional sections). The method does not throw.
cases.description: Validates that `apply` works for a completely empty DNS message and that the full‑signature flag does not cause an out‑of‑bounds error.

group: Message with only answer section and fullSignature false

input.value: Message that contains an answer section but no question section
valid TSIGRecord with algorithm HMAC_SHA512 and secret "ansonly"

cases.expected: TSIGRecord is added; the MAC is calculated over the DNS header and the (non‑existent) question section only, i.e., the header alone. The answer section is not part of the MAC.
cases.description: Confirms that when `fullSignature` is false the implementation follows RFC 2845 even if the message lacks a question section, ignoring the answer section.

input.value: Message with a question section; system clock set to a fixed Instant with nanosecond part 123456789
valid TSIGRecord with algorithm HMAC_SHA1 and secret "precise"

cases.expected: The generated TSIGRecord’s time‑signed field contains a value truncated to whole seconds (nanoseconds are zero). No exception is thrown.
cases.description: Ensures that `apply` normalises the timestamp to second granularity, as required by the TSIG specification.

input.value: TSIGRecord whose algorithm name is HMAC_SHA256 but the secret key is intended for HMAC_SHA1 (different key length)

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or GeneralSecurityException wrapped) thrown because the algorithm name does not match the secret key’s expected size/format.
cases.description: Checks that the method validates that the supplied algorithm is compatible with the secret key and fails fast on a mismatch.

group: Existing TSIGRecord present while old parameter is null

input.value: Message that already contains a TSIGRecord with key "existing.example."

cases.expected: The existing TSIGRecord is replaced by a newly generated one (key name derived from the message’s TSIGRecord if possible, otherwise a default). No exception is thrown.
cases.description: Verifies that when `old` is null but the message already carries a TSIG, the method treats the attached record as the basis for re‑signing rather than throwing an error.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException thrown because TSIGRecord.keyName is null
cases.description: The apply method must validate that the key name inside the supplied TSIGRecord is not null; supplying a record with a null key name should result in an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: NullPointerException (or IllegalArgumentException) thrown because TSIGRecord.algorithm is null
cases.description: When the algorithm field of the supplied TSIGRecord is null, apply should fail fast, throwing a NullPointerException or IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException thrown because TSIGRecord.secret is null
cases.description: The secret key byte array inside TSIGRecord must not be null; the method should detect this and throw an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException thrown because algorithm name is empty
cases.description: An empty algorithm name cannot be mapped to a MAC implementation; apply should reject it with an IllegalArgumentException.

group: Unsupported MAC algorithm despite valid name format

cases.expected: GeneralSecurityException (wrapped in IllegalArgumentException) thrown because the JCE provider does not support the requested MAC algorithm
cases.description: Even though the algorithm string follows the "HMAC-…" pattern, the underlying JCE does not provide an implementation; apply should surface the resulting NoSuchAlgorithmException as a GeneralSecurityException or IllegalArgumentException.
